pr_title: Fix raw_post raising when rack.input is nil
pr_body:
### Motivation / Background

Fixes #52125

### Detail

Starting in Rack 3.1, rack.input is optional, so `read_body_stream` (used by `raw_post`) can no longer call `read` unconditionally.

* [x] Tests are added or updated if you fix a bug or add a feature.
* [x] CHANGELOG files are updated for the changed libraries if there is a behavior change or additional feature. Minor bug fixes and documentation changes should not be included.
pr_comments: Rebased and fixed the Action Mailbox controller. As I mention in the commit message, this doesn't appear to be testable inside `IntegrationTest` at the moment. It seems like `rack` and/or `rack-test` needs to be updated to allow `rack.input` to be `nil` inside `IntegrationTest`.

Maybe this helps:

* `Rack::MockRequest.env_for` accepts an input option:
https://github.com/rack/rack/blob/0b6f760021e01b3031128e81536fc61cef676969/lib/rack/mock_request.rb#L142
* You can also pass in options to `MockRequest#request`: https://github.com/rack/rack/blob/0b6f760021e01b3031128e81536fc61cef676969/lib/rack/mock_request.rb#L66-L67
* We configure the MockRequest in rails here: https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/6045f257fbbff039edb2542c9859488cec0dcaa9/actionpack/lib/action_dispatch/testing/test_request.rb#L17-L21

So maybe you can pass it in your test? Or you can override `env[RACK_INPUT]`?

I'm not sure it helps, but it's nice if we have test coverage, I guess.

Thanks for working on this!

> Or you can override `env[RACK_INPUT]`

This worked 🎉 I rebased to fix the CHANGELOG conflict and now there is a working test for both places
Wow, thanks for fixing and releasing this one day before I ran into the issue! 🎉

issue_context.title: Some Rails integration tests break with rack 3.1
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce
Any reference to `request.raw_post` will trigger an exception during integration tests. The code works fine, as do system and controller tests.

Apparently this is due to the header 'rack.input' which has now become optional, and will be nil if there is no input: https://github.com/rack/rack/pull/1997

Rails should probably check for existence of that header (or lock to an older rack version)

### Expected behavior
No test failures

### Actual behavior
```
`NoMethodError: undefined method `read' for nil
           /ruby-3.3.1/gems/actionpack-7.1.3.4/lib/action_dispatch/http/request.rb:472:in `read_body_stream'
```

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 7.1.3.4

**Ruby version**: 3.3.1
comments: Can you provide a way to reproduce the error you are seeing? My app is running Rack 3.1 on Rails `7-1-stable` and I haven't seen any issues in any `ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest`s
@skipkayhil  Did you use `request.raw_post` in your code? That's all that's needed to reproduce it.

Here is the reproducible code.

```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require "bundler/inline"

gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"

  gem "rails"
end

require "action_controller/railtie"

class TestApp < Rails::Application
  config.root = __dir__
  config.hosts << "www.example.com"
  config.secret_key_base = "secret_key_base"
  config.action_dispatch.show_exceptions = :rescuable
  config.logger = Logger.new($stdout)
  Rails.logger  = config.logger

  routes.draw do
    get "/" => "test#index"
  end
end

class TestController < ActionController::Base
  def index
    request.raw_post
    render plain: "Home"
  end
end

require "minitest/autorun"

class TestControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest

  def test_returns_success
    get "/"
    assert_response :success
  end

  private
    def app
      Rails.application
    end
end
```
Thank you both for the reproduction! I think it makes sense that `raw_post` should continue to work (and return `nil`) when `rack.input` is `nil`, so I opened a PR to fix the issue.

review_comments: Is there anything else that calls `reset_stream`? It is private, so maybe we should move this into there to deal with nil?
Yes, you can move there. I actually refactored that code to fix this issue. I'm not sure only changing this method is enough. Rails has assumption that `request.body` will return something.

I felt like `read_body_stream` was an appropriate place to check for `nil` since `reset_stream` to me implies we are passing a (non-nil) `stream`, but I don't have a strong preference and am happy to move the nil-check into `reset_stream`.

Is the goal to have `body` always return a `StringIO` even though `rack.input` can be `nil` now? Or just that we need to handle that case in Action Mailbox?

>Is the goal to have body always return a StringIO even though rack.input can be nil now? Or just that we need to handle that case in Action Mailbox?

I'm not sure about the first question, but I would expect `create_and_extract_message_id!` to handle nil accordingly

https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/242216803ee73f528b0a74c6bdb367e5b98d8f83/actionmailbox/app/controllers/action_mailbox/ingresses/relay/inbound_emails_controller.rb#L55C1-L56C1
I think `body` can return `nil`, but our code should not rely on it never returning `nil`.
